# The generated client reaches a real reconciler, durable store and local
# executor. Workloads are Go test helper processes; no shell tools are needed.
taskfile success.json success
taskfile failure.json failure
taskfile hold.json hold

skygo plan -f success.json
stdout '^local\n$'
skygo --json jobs list
! stdout '"id"'
skygo --json run -f success.json --request-id first --wait
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED"'
stderr 'request-id: first'
job-id FIRST
skygo --json run -f success.json --request-id first --wait
stdout '"id": *"'$FIRST'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED"'
skygo jobs logs $FIRST
stdout '^hello from the workload\n$'
skygo --json jobs get $FIRST
stdout '"id": *"'$FIRST'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED"'
skygo --json jobs list
stdout '"id": *"'$FIRST'"'

# A changed payload cannot reuse the binding, and a failed workload exits 2.
! skygo run -f failure.json --request-id first
stderr 'already_exists'
env SKYGO_EXIT_CODE
stdout '^SKYGO_EXIT_CODE=1\n$'
! skygo --json run -f failure.json --request-id failure --wait
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_FAILED"'
stdout '"exit_code": *7'
stderr 'request-id: failure'
env SKYGO_EXIT_CODE
stdout '^SKYGO_EXIT_CODE=2\n$'

# Wait for the Go process itself before canceling, then retry the submission
# with --wait to observe terminal cancellation of the same durable job.
skygo --json run -f hold.json --request-id hold
job-id HOLD
ready
! skygo jobs cancel $HOLD
stderr 'requires --yes'
skygo jobs cancel $HOLD --yes
! skygo --json run -f hold.json --request-id hold --wait
stdout '"id": *"'$HOLD'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_CANCELED"'
env SKYGO_EXIT_CODE
stdout '^SKYGO_EXIT_CODE=2\n$'
skygo jobs logs $HOLD
stdout '^workload is running\n$'
